title: Correct readiness dimension assignment and capability ownership checking
description:
Decomposed out of eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1 (PR #475) 2026-07-26 under the churn stop
rule. These are bounded, mechanical defects that do not belong in the design
reopening and can be fixed independently.

From the fresh full review of 8c027f1:
 * Capability failures are assigned to PROJECTED rather than SUPPORTED. A clause
   whose engine capability is unresolved is reported as a projection defect,
   which is precisely the CAPTURED/PROJECTED/SUPPORTED/DISCOVERABLE conflation
   ADR 0020 exists to prevent.
 * Capability ownership is checked with an INCORRECT bead-ID prefix, so
   wrong-owner references pass.
 * Evidence and provenance consistency remain under-validated.
 * Branch and alternative bindings can target shells but cannot target several
   valid scalar mechanics.
 * ADR 0020 contradicts the updated bead contract about the #475/#477
   integration boundary — the ADR must state the actual position, which is that
   #475 and #477 share obl:::<sourceRef>:::<locator>:::<facet> while #476 does
   not participate.

Keep this bead narrow. If a fix here starts requiring exact source values, it
belongs to the sibling source-value bead instead.
acceptance_criteria:
• Capability resolution failures are reported against SUPPORTED, never PROJECTED, with a test per dimension.
• Capability ownership uses the correct bead-ID form; wrong-owner references fail.
• Evidence and provenance consistency are validated.
• Branch and alternative bindings can target scalar mechanics, not only shells.
• ADR 0020 states the real cross-PR integration position and does not contradict the bead contract.
close_reason: Implemented in efde702 on PR #475 branch; supervisor-verified 4743 passed, 19 skipped.
